Product UX · Tablet ordering

Rose Family Bakery POS

A point-of-sale ordering flow that keeps a custom order visible while staff work through its details.

Explore the designs ↓
My role
UX & wireframe design
Tools
Figma
Deliverable
Low- and mid-fidelity tablet interfaces

THE PROJECT

Overview

Custom bakery orders combine product selection, personalization, timing, and payment. This tablet concept organizes those decisions into a staged flow and uses a persistent order summary to keep the current order in view.

01 / DESIGN PROCESS

Give a complex order a clear structure

The low-fidelity screens establish a dashboard and a five-stage order flow, covering setup, products, review, customer and payment details, and confirmation. The ordering rules include at least 48 hours of lead time and scheduling up to 60 days ahead.

02 / DESIGN PROCESS

Keep customization within the order

The mid-fidelity work develops order type, product categories, and custom cake options. Size, flavor, theme, quantity, and a message of up to 50 characters sit alongside the current order. The layout gives staff a place to check the order while configuring a product.

03 / DESIGN PROCESS

Create a deliberate review step

The review screens bring the selected items, edit and remove actions, subtotal, delivery, and total together before payment. Comparing the low- and mid-fidelity stages shows the development of this information hierarchy. Confirmation closes the flow with an explicit completion state.

REFLECTION

What this work shows

This project demonstrates how a detailed service task can become a structured interface: stage the decisions, preserve the order context, and provide an opportunity to review. The supplied work is wireframe design, without documented testing results.

Academic concept. Original files: Bakery app stage 1 low fidelity wireframe.fig and Bakery app stage 2 mid fidelity .fig. Placeholder image areas are part of the original wireframes.
